translation: Pallavi (Chorus): Walking along so softly, O sister-in-law, walking along so daintily, O sister-in-law... Did my hand brush against you, O sister-in-law? Are you cross because my hand touched you, sister-in-law? Don't scold me, oh, O sister-in-law... Don't beat me, oh, O sister-in-law... I'll bow at your feet, O sister-in-law... I'll bow to your hands, O sister-in-law... (Walking along so softly, O sister-in-law, walking along so daintily, O sister-in-law) (Did my hand brush against you, O sister-in-law? Are you cross because my hand touched you, sister-in-law?)

Verse 1: No saris, they're so dear, O sister-in-law... No blouses, they're so dear, O sister-in-law... I'll have saris brought for you, come along, my sister-in-law... I'll have blouses stitched for you, come along, my sister-in-law... (Walking along so softly, O sister-in-law, walking along so daintily, O sister-in-law) (Did my hand brush against you, O sister-in-law? Are you cross because my hand touched you, sister-in-law?)

Verse 2: No bangles, they're so dear, O sister-in-law... No toe rings, they're so dear, O sister-in-law... I'll have bangles brought for you, come along, my sister-in-law... I'll have toe rings brought for you, come along, my sister-in-law... (Walking along so softly, O sister-in-law, walking along so daintily, O sister-in-law) (Did my hand brush against you, O sister-in-law? Are you cross because my hand touched you, sister-in-law?)

Verse 3: No flowers, they're so dear, O sister-in-law... No face powder, it's so dear, O sister-in-law... I'll have flowers brought for you, come along, my sister-in-law... I'll have powder brought for you, come along, my sister-in-law... (Walking along so softly, O sister-in-law, walking along so daintily, O sister-in-law) (Did my hand brush against you, O sister-in-law? Are you cross because my hand touched you, sister-in-law?) (I'll bow at your feet, O sister-in-law, I'll bow to your hands, O sister-in-law)
summaryEn:
This is a teasing, good-humoured family song sung by a young man to his vadina, his elder brother's wife. In Telugu village culture the relationship between a man and his brother's wife traditionally allows light-hearted joking and banter, and the song plays on exactly that. As she walks past gracefully, his hand seems to brush against her, and the chorus is his mock-anxious apology: is she angry, will she scold or hit him? He promises to fall at her feet and fold his hands before her to make peace.

In each verse he tries to win her over with gifts. Things are scarce and costly, he admits, but he will still get her saris and stitched blouses, bangles and toe rings, flowers and face powder. The list of women's adornments, from traditional toe rings to modern powder, gives the song a cheerful, everyday flavour. The form is built on steady repetition: every line ends with the call "O vadine," each verse follows the same pattern of "there are none" followed by "I'll bring them," and the bracketed chorus returns after every verse, making it well suited to group singing at family gatherings.

ఇది ఒక యువకుడు తన వదినతో, అంటే అన్న భార్యతో, సరదాగా ఆటపట్టిస్తూ పాడే కుటుంబ పాట. తెలుగు పల్లె సంస్కృతిలో మరిది-వదినల మధ్య సరసమైన హాస్యం, ఆటపట్టింపులు సహజంగా ఉంటాయి; ఈ పాట అదే బంధాన్ని ఆధారంగా చేసుకుంది. వదిన సన్నగా నడుచుకుంటూ వెళ్తుండగా తన చెయ్యి తగిలిందేమో అని, దానికి ఆమె కోప్పడిందా, తిడుతుందా, కొడుతుందా అని మరిది భయం నటిస్తూ పల్లవిలో క్షమాపణ అడుగుతాడు. ఆమె కాళ్ళు మొక్కుతానని, చేతులు జోడిస్తానని బతిమాలుతాడు.

ప్రతి చరణంలో కానుకలతో ఆమెను బుజ్జగించాలని చూస్తాడు. వస్తువులకు గిరాకీ ఉందని ఒప్పుకుంటూనే చీరలు తెప్పిస్తానని, రైకలు కుట్టిస్తానని, గాజులు, మట్టెలు, పూలు, పౌడర్ తెప్పిస్తానని మాట ఇస్తాడు. సంప్రదాయ మట్టెల నుండి ఆధునిక పౌడర్ వరకు ఆడవాళ్ళ అలంకరణ వస్తువుల జాబితా పాటకు రోజువారీ జీవితపు రుచిని ఇస్తుంది. ప్రతి పంక్తి "ఓ వదినే" అనే పిలుపుతో ముగియడం, ప్రతి చరణం "లేవు" అని మొదలై "తెప్పిస్తా" అని ముగియడం, ప్రతి చరణం తర్వాత పల్లవి తిరిగి రావడం వల్ల ఇది కుటుంబ వేడుకల్లో అందరూ కలిసి పాడుకోవడానికి అనువైన పాటగా ఉంటుంది.
